title: Setting Up a Bank Account in France
summary: Learn how to open a bank account and what documents you’ll need.
body_md:
### Setting Up a Bank Account in France
Opening a French bank account makes daily life easier — from paying rent to receiving your salary.

#### 🏦 Recommended Banks
- **BNP Paribas**, **Société Générale**, **Crédit Agricole**, and **La Banque Postale** have strong local presence.
- Online banks like **Hello Bank**, **Boursorama**, and **Revolut** are also convenient for students and expats.

#### 📋 Required Documents
- Passport or residence permit  
- Proof of address (rental contract, utility bill, or housing certificate)  
- Proof of income or student enrollment  
- Visa or residence card (if applicable)

#### 💡 Tips
- Ask for a **RIB** (Relevé d’Identité Bancaire) for transfers and payments.
- International transfers are easier with **Wise** or **Revolut**.

title: Phone, SIM & Internet Setup
summary: How to get a French phone number and internet access.
body_md:
### Phone, SIM & Internet Setup
Having a local number helps with everything from job applications to setting up accounts.

#### 📱 Major Providers
- **Orange**, **SFR**, **Bouygues Telecom**, and **Free Mobile**.
- **Free Mobile** offers affordable plans — €19.99/month for unlimited calls and 210 GB data.

#### 🪪 What You’ll Need
- Passport or residence card  
- Proof of address (rental or CROUS contract)

#### 💡 Student Tips
- Prepaid SIMs work immediately but long-term plans are cheaper.  
- Wi-Fi is widely available in cafés, libraries, and university buildings.

title: How to Find Housing in Rennes
body_md:
### Recommended Neighborhoods
- **Centre**: vibrant, central, and full of life.
- **Thabor**: elegant, green, and calm near Parc du Thabor.
- **Saint-Hélier**: central and convenient.
- **Jeanne d’Arc**: quiet and residential.
- **Arsenal-Redon**: good value, near city center.

### Areas to Visit Carefully
- **Kennedy** and **Maurepas** — affordable but further from the center.

### Rental Prices (approx.)
| Type | Average Monthly Cost |
|------|-----------------------|
| Studio | €400–€600 |
| 1-bedroom | €550–€800 |
| Shared flat | €350–€500 |
| Student residence | €250–€450 |

### Useful Links
- [Le Bon Coin](https://www.leboncoin.fr/)  
- [SeLoger](https://www.seloger.com/)  
- [Studapart](https://www.studapart.com/)  
- [CROUS Rennes](https://www.crous-rennes.fr/logements/)

title: Getting Around Rennes
summary: How to navigate public transport and commute efficiently
body_md:
### Public Transport in Rennes
The **STAR network** runs buses and metro lines throughout the city.

#### 🚇 Metro
- **Line A**: North–South (Kennedy ↔ La Poterie)  
- **Line B**: East–West (Cesson–ViaSilva ↔ Saint-Jacques–Gaîté)

#### 🚌 Bus
Covers all main neighborhoods with reliable schedules.

#### 💳 Tickets & Passes
| Type | Price | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| Single ticket | €1.70 | Valid for 1 hour |
| Student monthly pass | €17 | Unlimited travel (with proof of enrollment) |
| Regular monthly pass | €25 | Unlimited travel |

Recharge or buy your **KorriGo card** at metro stations or [star.fr](https://www.star.fr).

title: Accessing Healthcare in Rennes
body_md:
### Getting Health Coverage
Register for **Sécurité Sociale Étudiante** at [etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr](https://etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr).

#### 🏥 Where to Go
- **CHU Rennes (Pontchaillou)** — main public hospital  
- Local **pharmacies** marked by green crosses  
- **SOS Médecins** for home visits  

#### 🩺 Private Health Insurance
Consider a **mutuelle** for extra coverage beyond Sécurité Sociale.

#### 🚨 Emergencies
- **112** — General emergency number  
- **15** — SAMU (medical emergencies)  
- **18** — Fire department  
- **17** — Police

title: Legal Paperwork & Residency
summary: Visas, OFII validation, and required documents
body_md:
### Arrival Checklist
- Validate your **visa** within 3 months via [administration-etrangers-en-france.interieur.gouv.fr](https://administration-etrangers-en-france.interieur.gouv.fr)
- Register for a **residence permit** if staying more than one year.
- Bring your **rental contract**, **passport**, and **proof of income** for most processes.

#### 🧾 Other Procedures
- Register for social security and get a **Numéro d’Assurance Maladie**.  
- Update your address with all institutions when you move.

title: Cost of Living in Rennes
summary: Budget breakdown for a comfortable stay
body_md:
### Average Monthly Budget
| Expense | Estimated Cost |
|----------|----------------|
| Rent (studio) | €500–€650 |
| Groceries | €200–€300 |
| Transport (KorriGo pass) | €17–€25 |
| Utilities & Internet | €80–€120 |
| Leisure | €100–€150 |

#### 💡 Tips
- Student discounts available via **ISIC** and **Carte Jeune**.  
- Markets like **Marché des Lices** offer affordable local food.  
- Cooking at home saves a lot!
